momentum_signals.description: Combined 2026 capex guidance from Alphabet ($175-185B), Meta ($115-135B), Amazon ($200B), and Microsoft exceeds $500B. NVIDIA guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $78B, implying continued sequential growth. AI infrastructure spending is translating into accelerating cloud revenue: Azure +39%, Google Cloud +48%, AWS +24%.

Salesforce Agentforce reached $800M ARR (+169% YoY) consuming 20 trillion tokens. Accenture AI bookings nearly doubled to $2.2B. Jensen Huang declared 'the agentic AI inflection point has arrived.' Companies shifting from generative AI experimentation to autonomous agent deployment at enterprise scale.

Global M&A volume hit ~$5T in 2025 (+40% YoY). Goldman Sachs posted record revenue of $58.28B; Morgan Stanley IB revenue surged 47%; JPMorgan equities trading +40%. Goldman CEO Solomon noted they are 'not yet in the middle of the potential for a full-on M&A cycle,' suggesting significant upside remains.

Eli Lilly's Mounjaro reached $22.97B full-year revenue (+99% YoY) and Zepbound $13.54B (+175% YoY). Lilly guided 2026 revenue to $80-83B (+25%). Medicare obesity coverage expansion represents a 'big multiplier on the eligible pool.' Amgen's MariTide entering late-stage development as next-gen competitor.

AEP contracted 56 GW incremental load by 2030 (doubled from 28 GW prior disclosure). Utilities sector planning $208B in grid upgrades for 2025 and $1T+ through 2029. Constellation Energy acquired Calpine and secured DOE loan for Crane nuclear restart. OpenAI 1.2 GW Stargate campus and Amazon 1 GW Indiana data center driving unprecedented utility demand.

Consumer Discretionary posted -3.5% earnings growth, the weakest of all sectors. PepsiCo cut snack prices up to 15%. Home Depot CEO said 'customers are telling us they're not investing.' McDonald's leaned into value with Extra Value Meals targeting low-income diners. Housing turnover at historical lows is suppressing home improvement spend.

Consumer Staples and Industrials had the highest percentage of earnings calls citing tariffs. P&G quantified a $400M tariff impact for fiscal 2026. Analysts cut Q1 2026 S&P 500 EPS estimates by 1.5% in Jan-Feb, the first such cut since Q2 2025. Front-month WTI dipped to ~$55/bbl partly on trade uncertainty.

RTX achieved record backlog of $268B including $107B in defense awards. Industrials sector earnings surged 27% YoY vs initial expectation of -0.3%, driven primarily by aerospace/defense. GE Aerospace and RTX leading with double-digit revenue growth. Global defense budgets expanding amid rising geopolitical tensions.

Energy was one of only two sectors reporting YoY earnings decline (-1.7% to -2.8%). Crude oil averaged $11/bbl lower than prior year period with WTI in the $55-60 range. Global crude surplus persists despite geopolitical tensions. SLB faces subdued international E&P spending outlook.

Netflix crossed 325M subscribers with operating profit growth ~30% and ad revenue exceeding $1.5B (expected to double to ~$3B in 2026). Disney DTC swung from $4B annual loss to $375M quarterly profit. Leadership rotating from subscriber growth metrics to profitability and ad-tier monetization.

Merck guided 2026 EPS of $5.00-5.15 vs $8.98 in 2025 as Keytruda LOE approaches and Gardasil sales fell 40%. AbbVie navigated the Humira cliff with Skyrizi/Rinvoq at $25.9B combined (+$8B YoY). The market is actively repricing pipelines as $150B in annual pharma revenues face patent expiration by 2030.

Magnificent Seven delivered +27.2% YoY earnings growth in Q4, contributing 66% of S&P 500 total EPS growth. The remaining 493 companies posted only 9.8% growth, below Q3's 12.2%. This widening divergence raises concentration risk concerns as Q1 2026 estimates are being cut for the broader market.
